text.p: Ameristar Casinos Inc said it has settled the arbitration proceeding against two former stockholders of Gem Gaming Inc.

On March 26, Ameristar began a proceeding against former Gem shareholders Steven Rebeil and Dominic Magliarditi, alleging that the pair breached the merger agreement under which Gem was acquired by Ameristar in October 1996.

Pending approval by the Nevada Gaming Control Board and the Nevada Gaming Commission, the settlement agreement provides for prinicipal payments totaling $32,650,000, of which $4,000,000 is to be paid at closing.

Ameristar said notes will be issued for the remaining principal balance carrying an interest rate of eight percent a year. Principal reduction payments of up to $3 million annually will be required beginning in November 1998, and the notes will mature on December 31, 2004.
The notes are prepayable without penalty, Ameristar said, and the notes will be subordinated to up to $250 million in indebtedness selected by Ameristar.
Ameristar also said that in accordance with the settlement, it will transfer back to a Gem affiliate Ameristar's interest in aircraft and hanger facilities acquired in connection with the merger.
